characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Conventional constant acceleration Doppler velocity drive with 57Co (Rh-matrix) source; transmission geometry; velocity of the drive calibrated by a pure iron (α-Fe) foil; spectra fitted with the NORMOS program (B_hf probability distribution up to 40 sextets).
characterization_methods.key_findings: The Fe-5Al Mössbauer spectrum was deconvoluted (NORMOS) into two components: B_hf = 32.67 T with area 24% and V_f 23.55% (assigned (8Fe)nn + (5Fe+1Al)nnn), and B_hf = 30.65 T with area 51.6% and V_f 50.7% (assigned (7Fe+1Al)nn + (6Fe)nnn or (8Fe)nn + (6Al)nnn). The P(B_hf) hump is broad and deconvoluted into multiple peaks spanning roughly 26–34 T. The hyperfine field decreases as the number of Al nearest neighbours increases (non-magnetic Al). The ~23 T peak observed for Fe-6Al, Fe-6.8Al and Fe-9Al (possible Fe3Al indicator) is ABSENT for Fe-5Al, attributed to a low volume fraction of the Fe3Al phase.
characterization_methods.purpose: Examine the local atomic configurations of Fe in the Fe-5Al powder sample and detect ordered-phase (DO3) formation / solid solution of Al.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Laboratory-based dual energy Mo-Cr-SAXS system (Xeuss, Xenocs, France); dual X-ray energies and camera lengths of 550 and 2400 mm; powder sandwiched between Scotch Magic tape (3M, USA); 2D profiles azimuthally integrated to 1D using FIT2D software; intensities converted to absolute scale with glassy carbon secondary standard; scattering angle calibrated with Silver-Behenate powder.
characterization_methods.key_findings: A weak nano-sized ordered-phase scattering peak is observed between q = 0.3–3 nm⁻¹. For the 5 wt% Al (Fe-5Al) composition, the Fe3Al ordered-phase diameter is ~2.5 ± 0.15 nm and the volume fraction is just below 0.5%. At low q (below 0.3 nm⁻¹) the intensity decays as q⁻⁴ (Porod scattering), assigned to larger heterogeneities (grains/grain boundaries); at high q (> 3 nm⁻¹) an incoherent flat background appears. SAXS volume fractions are lower than the Mössbauer-traced DO3 fractions.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Transmission geometry; measurement time 4–6 h; q-range from 0.0254 to 10 nm⁻¹
characterization_methods.purpose: Quantitatively estimate the size, volume fraction and number density of the ordered DO3 (Fe3Al) phase in the Fe-5Al powder sample.

analytical_models.equation_role: Relates the observed hyperfine field B to the number of Al atoms in the first and second nearest-neighbour shells: B = B0 - n1·ΔB1 - n2·ΔB2 (Eq. 1)
analytical_models.model_name: Hyperfine field – local atomic configuration relation
analytical_models.model_note: n1 and n2 are the number of Al atoms in the first and second nearest-neighbour shells; ΔB1 and ΔB2 values taken from Ref. [26].

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: B_hf distribution consists of up to 40 sextets
computational_details.simulation_method: Mössbauer spectrum fitting / deconvolution of the hyperfine magnetic field (B_hf) probability distribution
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Fitted B_hf distributions reproduce the experimentally measured Mössbauer spectra of the Fe-Al compositions and the α-Fe foil reference.

analytical_models.equation_role: I(q) = Δρ²·d_N·∫N(r)[V(r)F(q,r)]²dr (Eq. 2); N(r) log-normal distribution (Eq. 3); average size D_ave = 2·r_p·exp(w²/2) (Eq. 4); spherical form factor F(q,r) (Eq. 5)
analytical_models.model_name: SAXS intensity model for ordered phase
analytical_models.model_note: Δρ is the scattering length difference between the Fe3Al (DO3) ordered phase and the disordered Fe-Al matrix; d_N is the number density; r_p and w are the peak radius and standard-deviation of the log-normal distribution.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Spherical form factor for the DO3 ordered phase; log-normal number-density distribution of ordered-phase radii
computational_details.simulation_method: Nonlinear curve fitting of SAXS intensity profiles I(q) using a local mono-disperse model with a log-normal size-distribution of spherical ordered domains
computational_details.software_used: FIT2D software (azimuthal integration of 2D-SAXS profiles); nonlinear curve fitting of I(q)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Fitted curves (solid lines) agree well with the experimental SAXS intensities for the Fe-Al compositions including 5 wt% Al.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Charges consisting of interstitial free (IF) steel and pure aluminium were melted in a vacuum arc furnace to prepare the Fe-5Al low-density steel (5 wt% Al). The obtained circular buttons of diameter 10 cm and height 5 cm were re-melted multiple times (7–8 times) to remove segregation.
Samples for Mössbauer spectroscopy and SAXS were prepared by filing the alloy to obtain powders; filing generates internal stress in the powder particles.

processing_steps.atmosphere: high vacuum (10^-5 mBar); powder wrapped in a copper foil and sealed in a glass tube
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The (5 wt% Al) powder sample was wrapped in a copper foil and sealed in a glass tube under high vacuum (10^-5 mBar) and annealing was performed at 600 °C for 60 min. The sample was annealed to remove the internal stress generated during the creation of powder particles by filing.

phases_present.morphology: nano-sized, spherical (spherical form factor assumed in the SAXS model)
phases_present.volume_fraction: just below 0.5 % (5 wt% Al, SAXS; lower than the DO3 volume fraction traced by Mössbauer spectroscopy)

precipitates.distribution: nano-sized ordered phase dispersed in the ferrite matrix; gives a weak SAXS scattering peak between q = 0.3–3 nm⁻¹ (5 wt% Al)
precipitates.type: Fe3Al ordered phase (DO3, Fe-Al ordered phase)

microstructure_list.region: bulk (powder particles of the Fe-5Al steel)

structures.overall_structure: Polycrystalline, single-phase ferrite (BCC, disordered Fe-Al matrix) containing nano-sized Fe3Al ordered phase with DO3 structure; stabilisation of the single ferrite phase upon Al addition (5 wt% Al).

unmapped_findings: For the Fe-5Al powder sample the ~23 T Mössbauer hyperfine-field peak (observed for Fe-6Al, Fe-6.8Al and Fe-9Al and taken as a possible indicator of Fe3Al phase with low volume fraction) is absent, which the authors attribute to the low volume fraction of Fe3Al phase in Fe-5Al (b0047).

The Fe-5Al sample, like the other Fe-Al compositions, shows a broadened six-line Mössbauer sextet relative to the α-Fe foil, evidencing that Al addition alters the local Fe atomic configurations and creates new lower hyperfine-field components (figure_001, b0047).

SAXS scattering intensity of the Fe-Al low-density steels increases with Al content (5→9 wt%) implying an increase of the nano-sized ordered phase, and the Guinier regions shift towards low q confirming increasing ordered-phase size; at low q (below 0.3 nm⁻¹) intensity decays as q⁻⁴ indicating larger heterogeneities such as grains/grain boundaries (b0050).

The SAXS volume fractions of the ordered phase are lower than the DO3 volume fractions traced by Mössbauer spectroscopy because SAXS gives collective information about ordered phase having a sharper boundary whereas Mössbauer traces all local environments including those with diffused boundaries (b0050).
